questions.q: What does a process map show that a plain requirements list does not?
options: The exact Salesforce object API names to use
The order steps happen in and every decision branch
The cost of building the automation
The names of every end user in the org
questions.explain: Two individually correct requirements can still describe a process that doesn't actually flow -- a map exposes that in a way a list can't.

questions.q: In the lightweight mapping notation this lesson teaches, what does a diamond represent?
options: A decision point with labeled paths
A single action
A final outcome only
An unrelated note
questions.explain: Diamonds mark branch points -- in the Mill Creek example, 'Days requested > 5?' and 'Manager approves?' are both diamonds.

questions.q: In the Mill Creek process map, what happens to a 3-day request (not over 5 days)?
options: It is automatically rejected
It is routed to the Sales Director
It is auto-approved, with no manager review needed
The map leaves it undefined
questions.explain: The map's 'No' branch off the 5-day decision explicitly routes short requests to auto-approval, closing a gap a list alone might leave ambiguous.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say mapping and the Lesson 11 approval-process design 'describe the same thing at two different levels of detail'?
options: Because they are unrelated techniques used for different purposes
Because maps replace the need for an approval process entirely
Because only one of the two techniques is ever used in practice
Every box on the map becomes a final action, and every diamond becomes entry criteria or an approval decision
questions.explain: The map and the eventual configured process are two views of the same design -- mapping first helps confirm nothing is missing before building.

questions.q: What is the next course in the Salesforce Administrator path after this one?
options: Salesforce Platform App Builder
LTV Customer Management System
Salesforce Flow Automation
There is no next course -- this is the final course in the path
questions.explain: LTV Customer Management System is the portfolio capstone that closes out the Salesforce Administrator path.
